message:
Hello—I received the email below from contracts, and I think some of the information may have been left incomplete.

Good Morning,

I hope you're doing well.

The necessary changes for each site's subcontractor agreement are listed below. After making the edits, please send us updated versions of every subcontractor agreement. We hope these details are helpful and make the process faster.

Harborview Preparatory Institute
Allocated Budget: $24,000
Page 9: Signature Required (subcontractor section)
Information Required:
Subcontract (Annex B, Page 5)
Salaries and wages support sheet

Schedule for Harborview Preparatory Institute:
Tuesday & Thursday
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM
10:15 AM - 11:15 AM
Start Date: September 9th
End Date: October 18th

Please complete the following agreement information for MS 284:

Allocated Budget: $31,500
Page 9: Signature Required (subcontractor section)
Information Required:
Subcontract (Annex B, Page 5)
Salaries and wages support sheet

Schedule for MS 284:
Wednesday & Friday
3:30 PM - 4:30 PM
4:45 PM - 5:45 PM
Start Date: September 10th
End Date: October 19th
What they returned is the allocated-budget information our message requested. I'll add it now and send the document back.
They're a little messy over there, but great—thanks.

Before I update the subcontractor agreements and prepare the salary/wages support sheets, Morgan, I want to resolve one issue so the documents don't get returned to us again.

For both sites, the allocated budgets in this email differ from the amounts I had on file:
- Harborview Preparatory Institute: the email lists $24,000, while my records show $7,250
- MS 284: the email lists $31,500, while my records show $7,250

Could you confirm which figures are correct? I can see a few possible explanations:
- The total budgets were updated or corrected, meaning $7,250 is no longer accurate
- $6,800 represented one subcontractor's portion of a larger site total, while $24,000/$31,500 represents the full allocation for each site
- Something else changed on the contracts side

Because they're requesting a salary and wages support sheet rather than only a total, I'll also need these details:
1\. The hourly rate(s) that should be used for staff under this contract
2\. The number of staff covered by each site's budget, whether that's just one subcontractor or a team

After those details are confirmed, I can calculate the wages support sheet from the schedule they provided—3 sessions/day, 3 days/week, across each site's stated date range—so the figures reconcile cleanly with the correct allocated budget. I can then finalize Page 9 and Annex B Page 5 for signature.
Didn't the example I gave make the salary and wages support sheet add up to the budget amount? I thought you had already filled out that sheet.

Because we charge per session, I find the "3 sessions/day, 3 days/week, for the date ranges given at each site" breakdown tricky. Our schedule doesn't always fit that format neatly; for example, across three weeks we might meet on only 1 day rather than 9. The grand total therefore comes from the total session count—for HPI, that is $9,450 (18 sessions x$525).
Our document already contained both the signature and the salary and wages support sheet. Are you sure that was the version you sent them?
My guess is that the site may have a total allocated budget of, say, 24,000, while this particular subcontract uses only 9,450 of it.
If the signature and the salary and wages support sheet are already complete, are the allocated budget and the start and end dates the only items still missing?

On Annex B Page 4, the only field still open is "Amount Allocated in the Budget." From what you described, $24,000 appears to be the right entry: that would be the school's full program budget, while our subcontract draws only $9,450 from it. If that interpretation is correct, I'll enter $24,000 and include the required brief explanation that the subcontract amount is lower than the full allocated program budget.

Before I finalize the document, can you confirm that $24,000 is correct?
Since that's the amount he gave in the email, using it seems to make sense to me.
Allocated amount
Weirdly, they hadn't told us beforehand; that information was new.
Check this
With the signature included and every field completed, the document is ready for your review.
It seems fine to me.
Please send the completed document now, then let us know whatever they say in response.
So that other clients can see it, could you post public feedback on the milestone you approved the other day?
Scroll upward in the conversation to find the feedback option.
yes!
Did you manage to locate the feedback control?
Hi, Morgan.

Could you make these revisions as well? Sorry, I have changes for these five budgets. For NCA, the allocated budget for NH is $18750; the start date was 9/8, and it ends on 10/20.

The site labeled 286R, which is actually 201, has a budget of $16200. They started on 9/3 and will also end on 10/22. She also said:

"The number of weeks served on Annex B Page 5 is incorrect. It is listed as 11.5 weeks, but the correct total is 7 weeks. Please update the number ASAP so we can ensure everything is accurate and the payments are correct."
Nca and Nh refer to the same school.
On it
The interface message cuts off after the opening quotation mark, so I can't tell where I'm supposed to submit the feedback.
Before requesting feedback, should I add the bill for this new one, or should the billing and feedback requests be handled separately?
Either approach works for me.
Regarding the pdf request, the current copy of 286R isn't readable. Could you resend the document as a docx?
Thank you

I can't complete the edits or finalize either document until you confirm the following details.

1\. Weeks correction (both NCA and 286R/201): On Annex B Page 5, changing the weeks column from 11.5 to 7 while leaving the hourly rates and hours unchanged would push both salary totals far below the current subcontract amounts. NCA would go from $12,650.00 to about $7,700 against an $18,750 total, while 286R/201 would fall from $10,925.00 to about $6,650 against a $16,200 total. Should I close those gaps by increasing the hourly rates or hours, or should I place the difference in a non-personnel line such as Consumable Supplies or Equipment, following the approach used for HPI and MS 284?

2\. 286R or 201: Please confirm which name belongs on the final document. The Contract ID # for this site is also blank; do you have it?

3\. NCA Contract ID #: This field is blank as well. Can you provide that number?

4\. 286R/201 Amount Allocated in the Budget field: Instead of a dollar amount, the field currently contains 65%. Should it show the site's full program allocation, as with HPI at $24,000 and MS 284 at $31,500?

5\. NCA dates: Two different ranges currently appear in the same document—the Term section shows 8/30/27 to 10/15/27, while the Schedule table shows 9/1/27 to 10/8/27. With the new dates set for 9/8 to 10/20, should both the Term line and Schedule table be updated to match, or does one of the existing ranges need to remain?

Once you answer these questions, I can finalize both documents.

1\. Follow the same approach used for HPI, but put the difference only in approved lines such as travel and consumable supplies. 2. Since she did not provide a contract ID, use 286R; it is confusing because the funding comes from one school while the program is hosted at another location. 3. The NCA contract ID is the same situation—it was not provided. 4. Use the numbers she supplied when I asked, although I don't think she knows the correct answer. 5. To keep everything consistent, apply the dates she gave us to all of the date fields. She has been especially difficult to work with and still hasn't supplied the information we need for our schedules, so hopefully the documents won't get kicked back again.
Check this

You signed the contractor section rather than the subcontractor section. Before I correct it, sign the subcontractor part for you, and send the document over, I need confirmation that this was a mistake.
That was definitely a mistake, so please go ahead and fix it if you can.
